text: Founded in 1885, Banff is Canada's first national park and part of the first national park system in the world.
Jasper is the largest national park in the Canadian Rockies, and the world's second-largest dark sky preserve.
Gros Morne is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its Tablelands are a rare outcrop of the Earth's mantle, pushed skyward about half a billion years ago.
Mount Robson stands 3,954 m tall, and few mountains anywhere offer nearly 3,000 m of uninterrupted ascent.
Kluane National Park and Reserve is home to 17 of Canada's 20 tallest mountains, including Mount Logan (5,959 m), the country's highest peak.
The West Coast Trail spans 75 km from Pachena Bay to Gordon River, in the traditional territories of the Huu-ay-aht, Ditidaht and Pacheedaht First Nations.
Algonquin Provincial Park was established in 1893 and covers 772,300 hectares.
Summer climbing camps at Garibaldi Lake led to a park reserve in 1920, and Garibaldi became a Class A park in 1927.
The Grouse Grind climbs 800 m in 2.5 km, with 2,830 stairs from base to summit.
In the traditional territory of the Saugeen Ojibway Nation, Bruce Peninsula National Park's towering cliffs of the Niagara Escarpment plunge into Georgian Bay.
Mount Assiniboine Park was set aside on February 6, 1922, as the seventh park in BC's park system, and was enlarged sevenfold in 1973.
The Stawamus Chief is one of the largest granite monoliths in the world, with 700-metre cliffs at the southern entrance to Squamish.
Killarney Provincial Park, established in 1964, is a 645 square kilometre wilderness park.
Lake Superior Provincial Park was established in 1944 and covers 160,810 hectares.
The Juan de Fuca Marine Trail follows 47 km of remote coastline along the western shoreline of southern Vancouver Island.
Cape Scott Park, established in 1973 at the northwestern tip of Vancouver Island, has more than 115 km of ocean frontage.
Kokanee Glacier Park was established in 1922, making it one of the oldest parks in British Columbia.
Sleeping Giant Provincial Park was established in 1944 and covers 24,400 hectares.
On the Healy Pass Trail, wildflowers bloom from mid-July to late August, and scattered alpine larches turn golden yellow in late September.
Pukaskwa National Park protects a remote granite shore along Lake Superior, with cliffs and secluded sandy beaches.
Following the Cabot Trail through Cape Breton Highlands National Park, forested river canyons carve into an ancient plateau edged by rust-coloured cliffs.
Yoho National Park protects Burgess Shale fossil sites, which you can explore on guided hikes.
